newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai trades one third of yuan interbank market.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai trades one third of yuan interbank market.

text.p: Shanghai's main money brokerage was the most active member of the nation's local currency interbank market in 1996, accounting for one third of the turnover on the market, the Business News said on Monday.
The Shanghai Short-term Fund Financing Centre, run by the People's Bank of China, traded a total of 178.4 billion yuan in 1996 against a market total of 587.2 billion yuan, the newspaper said.
The centre was one of the founding members of the interbank market launched one year ago to facilitate the movement of surplus short-term funds amongst banks in different parts of China.

The market now has 19 state banks and 35 short-term finance centres, money brokerages run by the central bank, as its members. Other financial institutions which need to borrow or lend short-term money must go through the members.
